subject: Fixing variances of latent variables with ordered=T

messages.author: 56a8aa4a45a311ff
messages.subject: Fixing variances of latent variables with ordered=T
parts:
Dear all,
I get this model with ordinal data where the std beta weight from one latent construct (made of ordinal items) to the other latent construct (also made of ordinal items) is greater than 1 (std.all = 1.15).

However, I get an estimate of 0.55 for R2 of the endogenous latent construct... I wonder How can that be?


I tried to fix the variance of "SatFam  ~~ 0.1*SatFam", but it does not do anything (I am also using parametrization="theta" to allow for the estimation of variances, but I guess that only works for ordinal manifest items).

Any idea how to fix the variance of latent endogenous constructs? or how can i get a R2 of .55 if the std.all weight is greater than one?

Thanks!!!

messages.author: 9b7a59c6f2d552cc
messages.subject: Re: Fixing variances of latent variables with ordered=T
parts:
Standardised beta weights in regression analysis like SEM or path analysis mean that for a 1 standard deviation change in the predictor (here BTF) you get a 1.15 standard deviation change in SatFam. It's allowed for a beta weight to be greater than 1 because it has to do with change in the SD not the mean. It's different to a correlation. 
But do you believe this result? That requires you to trust your data, your model, and have a theory to explain the causal mechanism the model demonstrates. 
but what you have is allowed.
